summary: Iteration 118 – origin/CORS auth fix (tejas/origins.py + server.py L72-94). The CODE fix is verified; the LIVE fix is still pending (production config and redeploy). (1) Unit tests: 70/70 passed for normalise_origin/configured_origins/origin_allowed. These cover whitespace, trailing /, case, default ports, de-duplication, explicit non-default ports and IPv6. They also cover rejection of null, empty values, paths, queries, fragments, userinfo, wildcard hosts, bad or out-of-range ports, control characters, hostile suffixes/substrings, and invalid configs failing closed without echoing values. (2) In-process ASGI tests with REAL auth (X-Test-User override cleared) on the isolated DB tejas_isolated_iter105_test, with config supplied only through the subprocess env. FIXED config (FRONTEND_URL=https://jeelive.ai/, CORS_ORIGINS=' * ,https://www.jeelive.ai, <preview>/ ,https://jeelive.ai:443'): 77 passed, 2 skipped (unused parametrised slots). .env preview config (preview FRONTEND_URL, CORS_ORIGINS='*'): 75 passed, 4 skipped. MISCONFIG reproduction (FRONTEND_URL=https://www.jeelive.ai, CORS '*'): 6/6 passed. In that run Origin https://jeelive.ai got 403 origin_denied for phone 0000000000 and staff {} before credentials were checked, the www origin got 422, invalid explicit configs raised RuntimeError at import without leaking the secret, and a legacy '*' alone did not crash the app. (3) Browser tests through a TEST-ONLY real-auth bridge on 127.0.0.1:8766 (playwright route.fetch). Misconfigured bridge: the UI showed 'Cross-origin write rejected.' for phone and staff, with no JS errors. Fixed bridge, desktop 1920x800 and mobile 390x844: invalid phone showed a readable message (no [object Object]); valid phone went to /home; cookies were HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/; the session survived a reload. Staff wrong password showed 'incorrect'; the correct password went to /studio and survived a reload. Logout went to /owner-login?next=/studio and /login?next=/home. A student opening /studio was redirected to owner-login. No pageerrors. (4) Public preview probes: preview origin gave 422 (phone and staff) and preflight 200 with exact ACAO + credentials; evil origin gave 403 and preflight 400 with no ACAO. (5) Read-only production probes: https://jeelive.ai with Origin jeelive.ai AND with Origin www.jeelive.ai both return 403 origin_denied for invalid phone and staff {}. www returns 308 to the apex. This is expected and not a regression: production still runs the old config/code. Customer DB unchanged: 222 sets, 15700 questions, 206 sessions, 1 attempt, 1 user, 3 phone profiles, 0 limit rows. Snapshot compare = SAME.

minor.issue: Malformed ports are accepted leniently. 'https://jeelive.ai:' (empty port) and 'https://jeelive.ai:0443' (leading zeros) both normalise to https://jeelive.ai. On Python 3.11, urlsplit.port also accepts non-ASCII digits. No new host becomes trusted, but the review request said malformed ports must be rejected. Fix: validate the port text with re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]{1,5}') and require it to be non-empty, with no leading zero unless the port is exactly 0 (port 0 is then rejected anyway).

The early return skips the security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Cache-Control no-store, X-Request-ID). This behaviour existed before the fix, but the 403 envelope now carries a request_id that has no matching header.

minor.endpoint: POST /api/auth/phone (phone shorter than 5 chars) and POST /api/auth/login {}
minor.issue: Returns the generic 'Request fields or values do not match this operation’s contract.' instead of a phone-specific hint. The UI shows it readably (no crash), but it is unhelpful for students. Pre-existing UX issue, not caused by this fix.

critical_code_review_comments: The CORS middleware (ExplicitOriginCORS.is_allowed_origin) and the unsafe-write fence (origin_allowed(origin, origins)) share the same list and the same normalisation. No regex, Host, X-Forwarded-Host, Forwarded or Referer trust exists; spoofing tests confirmed this.

protections is registered after add_middleware, so it is the outermost layer: disallowed unsafe writes get 403 before CORS or auth runs. OPTIONS preflight is not fenced and is handled by CORS, which returns 400 for unrelated origins. Order is correct.

The request side tolerates a trailing '/' and surrounding whitespace in the Origin header. This is harmless (exact host/port match is still required), but it is more lenient than the spec Origin syntax.
configured_origins raises RuntimeError chained from a ValueError whose message is generic, so configured values or secrets do not appear in tracebacks (verified).

Auth logic, roles, cookies, generation fencing, staff_auth_held, the 5-attempt lockout (6th attempt returns 429 + Retry-After, even with the correct password) and register 410 are all unchanged and verified with real auth.

rca of the issue: Production rejects every unsafe write from the canonical origin (403 origin_denied happens before credentials are checked) because the production FRONTEND_URL matches neither https://jeelive.ai nor https://www.jeelive.ai, and the old code did not honour CORS_ORIGINS='*'. I reproduced this in-process and in the browser with FRONTEND_URL=https://www.jeelive.ai. The new code normalises FRONTEND_URL plus an explicit CSV and ignores '*'. With FRONTEND_URL=https://jeelive.ai and CORS_ORIGINS=https://www.jeelive.ai, the flows work (verified). Mitigation: update the production env and redeploy. The slow first load from www SSL is out of scope; www currently returns 308 to the apex in about 0.2s and the TLS verify result was 0.
